title: SSL/TLS inspection rule order, predefined and default rules, limits

prose.text: Which SSL rule applies is a first-match question with three wrinkles: rules you did not write (predefined and default), read-only flags that break writes if echoed back, and a size ceiling on the rule set.

ascending-order.statement: SSL/TLS inspection rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order, top-down, and the first match decides.

quotes: Policy rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order (Rule 1 before Rule 2, and so on)
Rules are evaluated in a top-down, first-match style.

inspect-before-exempt.statement: To inspect something an exemption would otherwise cover, place an inspection rule before the exemption; for example inspect Client Connector device groups first, then exempt the locations.

quotes: If you need something inspected that is otherwise exempted, build an inspection rule before the exemption rule.
build one rule to inspect the Device Groups running Zscaler Client Connector and then another rule to exempt the locations or location group as necessary.

disabled-holds-slot.statement: A disabled SSL/TLS inspection rule is skipped but keeps its place in the rule order.

quotes: Disabling this option does not actively enforce the rule, and the service skips it and moves to the next rule. However, the rule does not lose its place in the rule order.

name-length.statement: A rule name can be at most 31 characters.

quotes: Enter a user-friendly name for the rule. The maximum length is 31 characters.
name (str): Name of the rule, max 31 chars.
evidence.after: Adds a new ssl inspection filter rule.

rule-cap.statement: The tenant can hold 255 SSL Inspection rules, made up of 245 custom and 10 predefined. The limits table lists no support-raise path for this row, unlike the 1,024 'All Other Policy Rules' row, which is annotated as raisable to 2,048 by contacting the Zscaler Account team.
rule-cap.conditions: Whether the cap is fixed or simply undocumented as raisable is gap cap-raisable.

quotes: 255 rules (245 custom rules and 10 predefined rules)
from 1,024 rules to 2,048 rules
| SSL Inspection Policy Rules | 255 rules (245 custom rules and 10 predefined rules) | |

| All Other Policy Rules (i.e., DLP Policy, Inline Web DLP Policy, IPS Control Policy, etc.) | 1,024 rules | Contact your Zscaler Account team for a possible increase in this limit from 1,024 rules to 2,048 rules. |

predefined-rules.statement: Zscaler ships predefined special rules: Zscaler-Recommended Exemptions (enabled by default), O365 tenant restriction inspection rules, an O365 One Click rule, a UCaaS One Click rule, and an Unauthorized Traffic Bypass for IoT Classifications rule. The help page calls them not editable, to be implemented as is, but they can be enabled or disabled. The IoT rule is disabled by default and cannot be deleted; for that rule only rule order, admin rank, status, label and the Evaluate/Bypass choice can change.

quotes: Zscaler provides the following predefined special rules which you can enable or disable based on your
These rules are not editable and can only be implemented as is.
Zscaler-Recommended Exemptions rule: Predefined rule to automatically exempt known destinations that cannot be SSL/TLS inspected. This rule is enabled by default.
O365 One Click rule: Predefined rule, controlled by the Microsoft-Recommended and Legacy Office 365 One Click setting.
This rule is disabled by default and cannot be deleted.
O365 tenant restriction inspection rules: Predefined rules to enable Office 365 Tenancy Restrictions for location and remote user traffic.
UCaaS One Click rule: Predefined rule, controlled by the UCaaS One Click configuration.
Unauthorized Traffic Bypass for IoT Classifications rule: Predefined rule to allow unauthorized traffic to bypass SSL/TLS Inspection for IoT classifications in all IoT policy-enabled locations.

You can modify the Rule Order, Admin Rank, Rule Status, Rule Label, and choose Evaluate Other Policies or Bypass Other Policies under Do Not Inspect Action for this rule and cannot edit other attributes.

default-rule.statement: The Leading Practices rule set ends with a Default rule whose action is Do Not Inspect with Evaluate Other Policies; 'inspect everything not exempted' is a separate Inspect All rule (criteria Any/Any/Any) placed above it.

quotes: New default. Inspect everything not exempted.
7 Inspect All Any/Any/Any Inspect
Do Not Inspect Default Default Rule N/A Evaluate other policies.

marker-fields.statement: `predefined` is a read-only boolean marking Zscaler's predefined SSL rules, `defaultRule` is a boolean marking the default rule (the contract does not mark it read-only), and `accessControl` is a read-only privilege (`NONE`, `READ_ONLY`, `READ_WRITE`) on the rule based on the admin's role-based access.

expect.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the rule is a predefined SSL inspection rule or not

evidence.note: predefined: readonly boolean, 'whether the rule is a predefined SSL inspection rule'

expect.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the rule is the default rule or not
Access privilege to this rule based on the admin's RBA

evidence.note: accessControl: readonly string, enum NONE, READ_ONLY, READ_WRITE

predefined-management.statement: Predefined SSL rules cannot be deleted; through the provider certain attributes such as description, state and labels can still be changed on them, though not all custom-rule attributes apply, and Default Rules must not be imported or managed because the API does not support managing them.

quotes: **NOTE 1** Zscaler SSL Inspection rules contain default and predefined rules which cannot be deleted.
**NOTE 4** DO NOT import or manage Default Rules. Management of default rules are not supported via the API.
Certain attributes on `predefined` rules can still be managed or updated via Terraform such as:
`description` - (Optional) Enter additional notes or information.
`state` - (Optional) An enabled rule is actively enforced.
`labels` (list) - Labels that are applicable to the rule.
not all attributes available on custom rules apply to them

strip-readonly-on-put.statement: The API rejects a PUT on a predefined SSL rule that carries the server-managed fields `predefined`, `defaultRule` and `accessControl` (the contract marks only `predefined` and `accessControl` read-only); the provider clears all three in its reorder callback, so a reorder that reads a rule and writes it back must do the same. Do not echo them back.
strip-readonly-on-put.conditions: Stated for reorder PUTs against predefined rules; the sources do not say whether a custom-rule PUT tolerates the fields.

quotes: The API rejects PUT requests for predefined rules when read-only fields (`Predefined`, `DefaultRule`, `AccessControl`) are included.

When the provider reorders rules, the `updateOrder` callback fetches each rule via GET and sends it back via PUT with the new order. For predefined rules, the API returns read-only fields that MUST NOT be included in the PUT body:
| ssl_inspection, firewall_filtering, firewall_dns, firewall_ips, nat_control, traffic_capture | `Predefined`, `DefaultRule`, `AccessControl` |
rule.Predefined = false
rule.AccessControl = ""
rule.DefaultRule = false
evidence.after: Strip read-only/server-managed fields so PUTs against

no-pagination.statement: The SSL inspection rule list returns every rule in one response; the Go SDK reads it with a single call because the API does not support pagination.

quotes: Use service.Client.Read directly since the API doesn't support pagination

name-truncation.title: What happens when automation sends a rule name longer than 31 characters
name-truncation.detail: Unverified legacy statement: 'Automation scripts that generate descriptive rule names from app metadata will silently truncate - names get rejected at rule-save time.' The two halves contradict each other (truncate versus reject) and no source shows which happens.

cap-raisable.title: Whether the 255 SSL Inspection rule cap can be raised through Support
cap-raisable.detail: The limits capture lists '255 rules (245 custom + 10 predefined)' with no raise annotation, while the adjacent 1,024 row says a possible increase to 2,048 is available by contacting the Zscaler Account team. Absence of an annotation does not prove the SSL cap is fixed. The old doc asserted 'NOT raisable' with no source.
cap-raisable.blocks: advising a large tenant to consolidate rules versus request a higher cap
